newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada changes T-bill auction schedule, maturities.
newsitem.headline: Canada changes T-bill auction schedule, maturities.

text.p: The Canadian government on Tuesday said it will begin holding T-bill auctions every other week rather than every week in an attempt to enhance liquidity in the market.
The government also said it will extend the maturity of three-month treasury bills by seven days. The changes will begin on September 18, 1997.

The measures take into account declining borrowing requirements and the shift to a higher proportion of fixed-income debt, the government said. It said the changes are based on extensive discussions with market participants and follow those initiated in 1993 and 1996 for the one-year and six-month T-bill issuance pattern.

"The success of federal debt management depends on a well-functioning domestic capital market and the new Government of Canada treasury bill issuance pattern will enhance the liquidity and efficiency of the market," Secretary of State for Finance Jim Peterson said.
The government said the measures will increase the size of the amounts auctioned at each T-bill tender and the outstandings for each bill maturity relative to the current auction pattern.
The new cycle will consist of:
- a new 98-day treasury bill at each bi-weekly auction.
- an initial 182-day offering followed by a re-opening of this bill (with 168 days remaining at the following T-bill auction.
- an initial 364-day offering followed by a reopening of this bill (with 350 days remaining) at the following auction.

The lengthening of the three-month term by seven days has the liquidity advantage of permitting outstanding six-month and one-year T-bills to be fundible with the three-month bills, the government said.

In order to support active trading, the government said the minimum tender sizes of T-bills will be announced two week prior to the auction with the final tender size announced one week prior to auction.
The government said the changes may require more frequent use of cash management bills to manage the its balances.
There will be a six-month transition phase when T-bills mature every week but regular auctions are held every second week.

"It likely will present some short-term technical difficulties, but on balance I think it's a positive development for the market," Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management Inc, said of the changes.
Posiewko said the news came as little surprise because of the government's widespread consultations with the industry.
